title: An isolated point of a fibre of a locally finite type morphism has finite residue field extension
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $x\in X$, put $s=f(x)$, and let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the fibre of $f$ at $s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. If the point of $X_s$ corresponding to $x$ is isolated in $X_s$ (the singleton is open in $X_s$), then the field extension $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$ induced by $f$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] is finite, i.e. $\kappa(x)$ is a finite-dimensional $\kappa(s)$-vector space [def-pc-field-extension].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01TH (morphisms-lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize, line 3664), (2) => (1), and Lemma 01TG (morphisms-lemma-residue-field-quasi-finite, line 3652); used in this form in the proof of More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM (more-morphisms.tex lines 12056-12059)

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Scheme.Hom.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_asFiber (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/QuasiFinite.lean:395) to the isolated fibre point. Since f is locally of finite type, its stalk map at x is quasi-finite. No change of the scheme or the point is necessary.

The quotient map from the stalk at x to its residue field is surjective (Scheme.residue_surjective), hence finite (RingHom.Finite.of_surjective) and quasi-finite (RingHom.QuasiFinite.of_finite). Compose it with the quasi-finite stalk map. Scheme.residue_residueFieldMap identifies this composition with the residue-field map composed with the quotient from the base stalk. RingHom.QuasiFinite.of_comp therefore makes the residue-field map itself quasi-finite. These are direct applications of Mathlib/RingTheory/RingHom/QuasiFinite.lean:37,42,51 and Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/ResidueField.lean:80,128.

Install the algebra structure induced by the residue-field map, as in the statement. Its quasi-finiteness is the result of step 2. Apply Module.Finite.of_quasiFinite (Mathlib/RingTheory/QuasiFinite/Basic.lean:141): the base residue field is a field, hence Artinian. Module.Finite over a field is FiniteDimensional, giving precisely the required extension.

proof_origin.place: Lemmas 01TH (2) implies (1) and 01TG, implemented directly using Mathlib quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_asFiber, the residue/stalk-map commuting identity, RingHom.QuasiFinite composition and cancellation, and Module.Finite.of_quasiFinite; no passage to fibre residue fields or tensor products.

Proof written in four steps: the fibre projection X_s -> Spec kappa(s) is locally of finite type (lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change) and x corresponds to a unique isolated point xi of X_s (def-pc-scheme-fibre); the field case, an isolated point of a scheme locally of finite type over a field has finite residue field (new node lem-weil-pbc-lft-over-field-isolated-point-residue-finite, Stacks Algebra 00PJ (1)=>(6) in an affine open, i.e. 01TH (2)=>(4) and 01TG for S = Spec k); kappa(x) -> kappa(xi) is an isomorphism over kappa(s) (lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field with Y = Spec kappa(s), kappa(x) tensor_kappa(s) kappa(s) = kappa(x) a field); finiteness transported.
